grades.quote: LR/SC can be used to construct lock-free data structures. An example using LR/SC to implement a compare-and-swap function is shown in Listing 2.
grades.reason: The passage shows that RISC-V's analogue to ARM's exclusive pair is LR/SC (lr.w and sc.w). It includes a retry loop that is the same pattern as LDREX/STREX. It doesn't mention ARM or locks explicitly. It gives a compare-and-swap example, which is the building block for a lock, so it only partly answers the question.

This passage is a set of textbook exercises on database transactions, isolation levels and two-phase locking. It has nothing to do with RISC-V load-reserved/store-conditional or ARM exclusive accesses.
